1.title: Division in the Church and the Wisdom of God
1.themes: Unity, the Cross as foolishness to the world, true wisdom, God's calling.
1.outline:
1. Greeting and Thanksgiving (1:1-9)
2. Divisions in the Church (1:10-17)
3. Christ the Wisdom and Power of God (1:18-31)
1.summary: Paul addresses the divisions among the Corinthians, reminding them that the message of the cross is the true wisdom and power of God, contrasting it with human wisdom.

2.title: Proclaiming Christ Crucified and Spiritual Wisdom
2.themes: Reliance on the Holy Spirit, divine vs. worldly wisdom, spiritual discernment.
2.outline:
1. Paul's message and demonstration of the Spirit (2:1-5)
2. The revelation of God's wisdom by the Spirit (2:6-16)
2.summary: Paul explains that he relied on the power of the Holy Spirit rather than eloquent speech. True wisdom comes from God's Spirit, which believers have received to understand God's thoughts.

3.title: Worldliness and Building on the Foundation of Christ
3.themes: Spiritual immaturity, divisions, the church as God's building and temple, judgment of believers' works.
3.outline:
1. Divisions as a sign of worldliness (3:1-9)
2. Christ as the only foundation (3:10-15)
3. The Church as God's temple (3:16-23)
3.summary: Paul rebukes the Corinthians for their fleshly immaturity. He portrays the church as a building founded on Christ, warning that every leader's work will be tested by fire, and affirms that believers are God's temple.

4.title: The Nature of Apostolic Ministry
4.themes: Stewards of God's mysteries, true apostleship, humility, spiritual fatherhood.
4.outline:
1. Servants of Christ and stewards of mysteries (4:1-5)
2. The apostles' humility contrasted with Corinthian pride (4:6-13)
3. Paul's fatherly warning and impending visit (4:14-21)
4.summary: Paul explains the apostles' role as humble servants and stewards, urging the Corinthians to imitate his humility rather than being puffed up with pride.

5.title: Dealing with Sexual Immorality in the Church
5.themes: Church discipline, purity, dealing with unrepentant sin, the Passover lamb.
5.outline:
1. A case of incest (5:1-5)
2. The necessity of purging out the old leaven (5:6-8)
3. Clarification on associating with the immoral (5:9-13)
5.summary: Paul commands the church to expel a member engaging in blatant incest, emphasizing the need for purity and the principle that a little leaven affects the whole batch of dough.

6.title: Lawsuits Among Believers and Sexual Purity
6.themes: Resolving disputes internally, avoiding lawsuits, bodies as temples of the Holy Spirit, sexual morality.
6.outline:
1. Lawsuits before unbelievers (6:1-8)
2. The unrighteous and the kingdom of God (6:9-11)
3. Glorifying God with the body (6:12-20)
6.summary: Paul scolds the Corinthians for taking each other to secular courts. He then strongly warns against sexual immorality, reminding them that their bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit.

7.title: Principles for Marriage and Singleness
7.themes: Marriage, celibacy, divorce, remaining in God's calling, the urgency of the times.
7.outline:
1. Instructions on marriage and sexual relations (7:1-7)
2. Instructions to the unmarried and widows (7:8-9)
3. Instructions concerning divorce (7:10-16)
4. Living as called (7:17-24)
5. The unmarried and the betrothed (7:25-40)
7.summary: Paul answers questions about marriage and singleness, advising both groups. He encourages fidelity in marriage and highlights the benefits of singleness for undistracted devotion to the Lord.

8.title: Food Sacrificed to Idols and Christian Liberty
8.themes: Christian liberty, avoiding stumbling blocks for weaker believers, love over knowledge.
8.outline:
1. Knowledge puffs up, love builds up (8:1-3)
2. The reality of idols and the one true God (8:4-6)
3. Forfeiting rights for the sake of the weak (8:7-13)
8.summary: Addressing food offered to idols, Paul argues that while idols are nothing, believers must not use their freedom in a way that causes a believer with a sensitive conscience to stumble.

9.title: Paul's Apostolic Rights and Self-Denial
9.themes: Apostolic rights, self-discipline, giving up rights for the Gospel, running the race.
9.outline:
1. Paul's rights as an apostle (9:1-14)
2. Paul's renunciation of his rights (9:15-23)
3. The need for spiritual discipline (9:24-27)
9.summary: Paul uses himself as an example of willingly giving up legitimate rights (like financial support) for the sake of spreading the Gospel, comparing the Christian life to an athlete's disciplined training.

10.title: Warnings from Israel's History and Fleeing Idolatry
10.themes: Learning from past failures, avoiding idolatry, doing everything for God's glory.
10.outline:
1. The example of Israel in the wilderness (10:1-13)
2. The incompatibility of the Lord's table and the table of demons (10:14-22)
3. Doing all to the glory of God (10:23-33)
10.summary: Paul warns against falling into the same sins as the Israelites in the wilderness. He urges the Corinthians to flee from idolatry and to prioritize the good of others, doing all to God's glory.

11.title: Propriety in Worship and the Lord's Supper
11.themes: Head coverings, order in worship, the significance and proper observance of the Lord's Supper.
11.outline:
1. Head coverings and gender roles in worship (11:1-16)
2. Abuses of the Lord's Supper (11:17-22)
3. The institution of the Lord's Supper (11:23-26)
4. Partaking in a worthy manner (11:27-34)
11.summary: Paul addresses propriety in public worship, focusing on head coverings. He then severely corrects their divisive and gluttonous practices at the Lord's Supper, reminding them of its sacred meaning.

12.title: Spiritual Gifts and the Body of Christ
12.themes: Diversity of spiritual gifts, unity in the church, the body of Christ, interdependence.
12.outline:
1. The varieties of spiritual gifts given by the same Spirit (12:1-11)
2. The church as one body with many members (12:12-31)
12.summary: Paul explains that the Holy Spirit gives diverse gifts for the common good. He illustrates the church as a physical body, where every member is essential and dependent on the others.

13.title: The Supremacy of Love
13.themes: Agape love, the necessity of love over gifts, the permanence of love.
13.outline:
1. The necessity of love (13:1-3)
2. The characteristics of love (13:4-7)
3. The endurance of love (13:8-13)
13.summary: Often called the "Love Chapter," Paul declares that even the greatest spiritual gifts are useless without love. He describes the enduring and selfless nature of true Christian love.

14.title: Prophecy, Tongues, and Order in Worship
14.themes: Edification of the church, the purpose of prophecy and tongues, orderly worship.
14.outline:
1. The superiority of prophecy over uninterpreted tongues (14:1-25)
2. Order and edification in church gatherings (14:26-40)
14.summary: Paul emphasizes that spiritual gifts must be used to edify the church. He prioritizes prophecy over uninterpreted tongues because it is understandable, and insists that all things in worship be done decently and in order.

15.title: The Resurrection of Christ and the Dead
15.themes: The gospel, the bodily resurrection of Jesus, the future resurrection of believers, victory over death.
15.outline:
1. The reality of Christ's resurrection (15:1-11)
2. The consequences if there is no resurrection (15:12-19)
3. The order of the resurrection (15:20-34)
4. The nature of the resurrection body (15:35-49)
5. The mystery of the transformation and victory over death (15:50-58)
15.summary: Paul defends the crucial doctrine of the resurrection. He proves Christ's resurrection, explains that believers too will be bodily resurrected with imperishable bodies, and celebrates the ultimate defeat of death.

16.title: The Collection for the Saints and Final Greetings
16.themes: Generosity, planning, mutual support, final exhortations, love.
16.outline:
1. The collection for the Lord's people (16:1-4)
2. Paul's travel plans (16:5-9)
3. Instructions concerning Timothy and Apollos (16:10-12)
4. Final exhortations and greetings (16:13-24)
16.summary: Paul gives instructions for a financial collection for the needy believers in Jerusalem, outlines his travel plans, and closes the letter with warm greetings and a final exhortation to stand firm in love.
